title: What an Effect is: syncing with outside systems

slides.text: Render, click… or just show up? 🛰️
slides.say: Components have two kinds of logic you know: rendering code and event handlers. Effects are the third kind.

slides.text: Rendering code: turns props and state into JSX. Must be pure.
slides.say: Rendering code takes props and state and returns JSX. It must be pure: just calculate, never do things.

slides.text: Event handlers: do things because the user did something, like a click.
slides.say: Event handlers do things, like sending a message, because the user did something specific.

slides.text: Effects: do things because the component is on screen, like connecting to a chat server.
slides.say: Effects do things caused by rendering itself. The chat is visible, so connect to the server. No click needed.

slides.text: Effects run after the commit, to sync with the network, browser APIs or other libraries.
slides.say: Effects run after React updates the screen. Use them to sync with outside systems. No outside system? You might not need one.
